record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.context_brief: non-iterative search of biological possibility space
record.original_question: Are there non-iterative physical mechanisms, other than generate-and-test evolution or growth and development, that can effectively explore the vast combinatorial state space of viable living forms—for example by quantum collapse to a viable candidate in a single step—or is an iterative process still required to prepare a state whose collapse has non-negligible probability of yielding a viable candidate?

evidence.quote:
Are there non-iterative processes that can effectively explore a Vast state space
of possibilities?

Are there physical mechanisms other than generate and test or growth and development, that could
be exploited in order to explore the Vast state space of possibilities more effectively, and in a non-iterative
manner? Could, for example, some form of quantum collapse to a viable candidate be possible in a single
step? Or would there still need to be some iterative process to arrange the superposition state into a
form where collapse yields a viable candidate with non-negligible probability?
These are open questions.

artifact.category_tag: quantum search of biological state spaces
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ denote the combinatorial state space of all candidate physical configurations of a living organism (for example, all sequences of biopolymers up to some bounded length, together with their spatial arrangements). Let $V \subset \mathcal{S}$ be the subset of configurations that are "viable" in the sense of corresponding to a self-maintaining living system, and assume $|\mathcal{S}|$ is "Vast" (e.g.\ super-exponential in the size of the organism) while $|V|/|\mathcal{S}|$ is exponentially small.

A \emph{search procedure} for $V$ is a physical process that, starting from resources (matter, energy, information) whose preparation cost is polynomial in the description length of an organism, outputs an element of $\mathcal{S}$. Call the procedure \emph{iterative} if it consists of a sequence of generate-and-test steps (as in Darwinian variation and selection) or of a developmental/growth trajectory whose length scales at least polynomially with the description length. Call it \emph{non-iterative} if it produces a candidate in $\mathcal{S}$ in $O(1)$ physical steps after preparation.

Question: Does there exist a physical (in particular, possibly quantum-mechanical) non-iterative search procedure that, with non-negligible probability, outputs an element of $V$? Concretely, can one prepare a quantum state $|\psiangle$ on a Hilbert space whose computational basis is indexed by $\mathcal{S}$, using only resources polynomial in the description length, such that a single projective measurement in that basis yields an outcome in $V$ with probability bounded below by an inverse polynomial? Or must any physical procedure achieving non-negligible success probability necessarily include an iterative preparation stage of length growing with the description length of viable organisms?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open conceptual problem at the interface of quantum physics, theoretical biology, and search complexity. No published mathematical or physical result is known to settle whether viable biological configurations can be reached by a genuinely non-iterative quantum process; standard quantum search lower bounds (e.g.\ BBBV) suggest unstructured search of a Vast space cannot be done non-iteratively, but no formal model of biological viability has been shown to fall under such bounds. Status remains open.

status_evidence.title: Quantum lower bounds by polynomials (BBBV / Beals et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes Omega(sqrt(N)) query lower bounds for unstructured quantum search, indicating that without exploitable structure quantum mechanics does not enable single-step search of a Vast space.
status_evidence.claim: Generic quantum search of an unstructured Vast space requires many queries, supporting that purely non-iterative quantum collapse to a rare viable candidate is not known to be achievable.

status_evidence.title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open question whether non-iterative physical mechanisms (e.g. quantum collapse) could explore the vast space of viable living forms.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly identified as open in the contemporary literature.
